agreement.metric: Spearman rank correlation on the common grid
agreement.scope: descriptive; CNN-ViT agreement is NOT evidence that either map is correct

auc.rule: trapezoidal over the 21 scored points including both endpoints

bootstrap.paired: methods compared on the same resampled image sets
bootstrap.quantities: every headline quantity, reported with 95% percentile CIs

deletion.fractions: equal steps of 5% from 0% to 100% of the 196 grid cells
deletion.order: descending map value; ties broken by ascending flat grid index
deletion.score: fused softmax probability of the locked target class

determinism.note: batch size changes float32 reduction order; the value actually used is recorded with the results

insertion.fractions: equal steps of 5% from 0% to 100% of the 196 grid cells
insertion.order: descending map value; ties broken by ascending flat grid index
insertion.score: fused softmax probability of the locked target class
insertion.start: fully masked image (all cells at the mask value)

masking.explanation: eval_transform normalises with mean 0.5 and std 0.5, so a raw mid-grey pixel of 0.5 maps to exactly 0.0 in tensor space; masking therefore replaces a region with the dataset channel mean
masking.rationale: nearest keeps each grid cell a hard-edged block so the masked fraction is exact; bilinear would blur the boundary and make the fraction approximate

method_set_divergence_from_adopted_plan: The adopted plan's X5 section lists ViT attention rollout and gradient-weighted ViT attention. Both were removed by the approved X3 amendment because they require eager attention, which failed the X2 neutrality gate. The ViT method evaluated here is the SDPA-safe Gradient x Input method verified in X2b and X3.

methods.source: X3 CNN Grad-CAM++ at native stage-8 resolution
X3 ViT patch-embedding Gradient x Input (the X2b method)

methods.note: formed in X5 only; X3 deliberately formed no composite
methods.source: 0.5 * norm(cnn) + 0.5 * norm(vit), both on the common grid

methods.gate_source: model(x, return_aux=True) gate from the same forward pass that produced the maps and the target class
methods.note: gate mass measures branch utilisation, not causal importance

methods.source: deterministic uniform random map, null baseline
deterministic isotropic Gaussian centred on the grid, sigma = grid/4, null baseline

normalisation.constant_map_policy: a map with max == min becomes all zeros and is recorded as degenerate; X4 established no real map is constant

prohibited_in_x5: any anatomical, tumour, lesion or clinical claim
any attention-based claim (no attention matrix is read)
treating CNN-ViT agreement as evidence of correctness
treating gate mass as causal importance
altering any locked parameter after observing a result
selecting the evaluated subset using faithfulness values
external or cross-source evaluation (that is Phase X6)
purpose: Quantitative faithfulness and stability evaluation of the X3 attribution maps. Locked before any faithfulness value is computed.

stability.map_comparison: Spearman rank correlation on the common grid, after inverting the geometric transform on the map

transformations.spec: additive Gaussian, sigma=0.01 in normalised tensor space, fixed seed 20260927

subset_decision.amendment_procedure: the decision is appended as a separate, separately hashed amendment; the original lock hash is never rewritten
subset_decision.decision_rule: taken from measured runtime and storage ALONE. Faithfulness values are not computed in the dry run, so the subset cannot be a function of the answer.

if_subset_required.recorded: every selected filename written into the amendment
if_subset_required.rule: stratified by true class, proportional allocation
if_subset_required.selection_time: before any faithfulness value is computed

subset_decision.status: OPEN at lock time - to be fixed by the dry run

target_class.note: the same target index is used for every method on a given image, so methods are compared on one decision
target_class.rule: predicted class from the recorded inference
